title: QL-1.04 The claims check runs in every repository from one script: a claim ahead of its status row fails CI
request: Closes quality-loop principle 4 (CI fails in any repo, site included, if a claim runs ahead of its row). Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-5.04. Quality-loop principle set of 30 October 2026 (owner's order: implement as a gate for all dev). Sequenced with QL-1.03, which also changes .github/workflows/ci.yml. The fixtures follow SR-5.04's status table as merged.

tasks.title: One claims checker
requirements: scripts/gate/claims.mjs reads the status table of SR-5.04 (docs/status.json, or the path given by --status) and scans the files given by --surfaces (globs) for each feature's claim phrases; a feature whose row is planned and appears without the planned label, or a performance figure without a results file named in its row, is a finding
a planned row without a date older than four weeks is a warning and older than eight weeks is a finding that says give it a date, drop it, or move it to the roadmap (principle 5)
--json prints {features, claims, findings, warnings}; exit 1 on any finding; no dependencies; a version: comment on the first line

claims.mjs exits 2, distinct from 1 for a finding, and prints the cause when the status file is missing, is not valid JSON, has no feature rows, holds a status outside the documented set, or has no claim phrases, and when a --surfaces glob matches no file; --json reports the number of files scanned
claims.mjs only reads files: it spawns no process, opens no network connection, writes nothing, and imports only node: built-ins and files beside it

a planned feature counts as labelled only when the label sits in the same sentence or HTML element as its claim phrase; 'not planned' and 'was planned' are not the label; phrases match without regard to case, across line wraps, with HTML tags stripped and entities decoded

a performance figure is a number with a unit of time, throughput or size (ms, s, MB, GB, ops/s, req/s, x faster) in a sentence; it needs a results file that exists, named in the row of the feature the sentence names, and a figure sentence that names no feature is a finding; version numbers and durations such as a 14-day trial are not figures
the age of a planned row comes from a field in the row (the date it was marked planned), never from a file time or git history; claims.mjs takes --now so tests fix the clock
the fixtures follow SR-5.04's status table as merged, and the CLI is tested end to end on fixtures at fixed paths

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/gate-claims.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T1-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest

criteria.statement: A fixture page claiming a planned feature without its label fails; the same page with the label passes; a planned row nine weeks old without a date fails and five weeks old warns

criteria.statement: claims.mjs exits 2 (distinct from 1 for a finding) and prints the cause in each of these cases: the --status file is missing; it is not valid JSON; it parses but has zero feature rows; a row's status is outside the documented set; the table has no claim phrases at all; any --surfaces glob matches no file. On the good fixture, --json reports the number of files scanned, and it equals the number of fixture pages.

criteria.statement: Two checks. (1) The test spawns claims.mjs under node --experimental-permission --allow-fs-read=<fixture dir>,<scripts/gate dir> (no fs write, no child_process, no workers) on the clean fixture and asserts exit 0 and the same --json output as an unrestricted run. (2) The permission model may not cover the network on the Node 22 line CI pins, so the test also reads claims.mjs and asserts that every import specifier starts with 'node:' or './', and that none of node:child_process, node:http, node:https, node:net, node:tls, node:dgram, node:worker_threads, fetch( or a dynamic import( appears.

criteria.statement: The fixture has three rows. Row A names results 'results/a.json', which exists; row B has no results; row C names a results file that does not exist. A page sentence giving A's phrase plus '12 ms' has no finding. The same sentence for B or for C gives one finding each, naming the row. A figure sentence that names no feature gives a finding. 'needs Node 22' and 'a 14-day trial' give no finding.

criteria.statement: 1. A Markdown fixture paragraph names two planned features, only one labelled '(planned)': exactly one finding, naming the unlabelled feature and its line. 2. The unlabelled phrase wrapped across a line break and in another case: still a finding. 3. 'is not planned' next to a claim: still a finding. 4. An .html fixture with the phrase split by inline tags and an  : a finding. The same HTML with the label inside the same element: no finding.

criteria.statement: With an injected clock (--now 2026-10-30) and the age taken from a field in the status row: undated rows at 3 weeks give nothing; at 5 weeks, one warning; at 9 weeks, one finding whose text contains 'give it a date, drop it, or move it to the roadmap'. A 9-week row with a date gives nothing. Copying the fixture into a new directory with no git history and a fresh mtime gives the same result.

tasks.title: Shipped to the other repositories
requirements: scripts/gate/sync-gates.mjs copies scripts/gate/** into a target checkout given by --to and prints the version of each file copied; a target whose copy is older than this repository's is reported
docs/DEVELOPING.md says the gate scripts are owned here and copied into memev-site, memev-cloud, memev-org and memev-ops, and that each of them runs claims.mjs in its CI
sync-gates.mjs copies docs/status.json with the gate scripts, and claims.mjs reads the status table only from the copy in its own checkout

sync-gates.mjs --check writes nothing and exits non-zero naming the file when a target gate file differs in content from this repository's (even at the same version line), is missing, or has no version line; versions compare numerically (1.10 is newer than 1.9), and a newer target copy is reported, never overwritten
memev's own CI runs claims.mjs over README.md, docs/**/*.md and site/**/*.html on every pull request that touches them and on a schedule, so the age rule runs even when nothing changes

each red-green criterion of this task that runs test/gate-sync.test.mjs has its own subtest whose name starts with <task>-cNN: (NN is the criterion's position in this task, so T2-c01: for the first), and the criterion runs only that subtest

criteria.statement: Syncing into a temporary git checkout writes every gate script with its version and reports an older copy

criteria.statement: The developing page names the four receiving repositories
The full suite passes

sync-gates.mjs --to <dir> --check writes nothing (the target's file hashes are unchanged afterwards) and exits non-zero, naming the file, when: a target gate file has the same version line but different sha256 content; a gate file is missing in the target; or the target copy has no version line. It exits 0 only when every file is byte-identical to this repository's. Residual risk that no criterion here can cover: a PR that edits its own copy is caught only if this check runs from outside that PR (a scheduled memev job over the four repositories, or CODEOWNERS on scripts/gate/** in each target).

criteria.statement: After sync-gates writes into a temporary git checkout that holds only a README.md, the test runs node scripts/gate/claims.mjs --json with cwd = the target, once through its realpath and once through a symlink to it. The README claims a planned feature without the label: exit 1, one finding naming README.md, features > 0. With the label added: exit 0. The status table is read only from what sync-gates put into the target, so the requirement must be amended to ship or reference the table.

criteria.statement: Once SR-5.04 has landed: run claims.mjs over this repository's own surfaces, in the form memev's CI uses. The real docs/status.json gives features > 0, claims > 0 and zero findings.

Target copies at version 1.9 against source 1.10, and a target copy with its version line removed, are both reported, with a non-zero exit or a 'stale' entry in --json.
